summary: Reuse the exact Stratic v2 logo for the desktop window and macOS Dock, copying the PNG into the build and retaining the SVG source.

examined.reason: The main-process icon setup does not alter selection validation, revision pinning or the session channel.
The build adds an app PNG alongside the existing assets. Markdown, KaTeX and project-image behavior and resources are unchanged.
No navigation or refresh code changes; only window creation and Dock identity use the copied logo.
The exact main-process source link now includes icon setup. Isolation, IPC sender checks and repository-content rendering are unchanged.
Adds the desktop icon promise and links startup and asset copying. Existing summaries still faithfully cover the main controls; no new control or label is added.
The existing native app now uses Stratic artwork. Reading, navigation, project selection and authority boundaries are unchanged.

results.method: npm run typecheck; npm run build; isolated Electron startup and native-image inspection; byte comparison with v2; node src/cli.ts validate
results.evidence: Typecheck and build exited 0. The built app opened its reader, loaded a nonempty 512x512 icon, and had a visible Dock entry. SVG and PNG match v2 byte-for-byte; dist PNG matches the source PNG. Validation found no issues. Logs are /private/tmp/stratic-icon-typecheck.txt, /private/tmp/stratic-icon-build.txt and /private/tmp/stratic-icon-startup.txt. This is a focused startup check, not a claim that the unit or full desktop suite ran.

unmapped.reason: The unmapped changed region is a separating blank line before the linked icon-copy statement.
Binary app artwork copied byte-for-byte from the v2 desktop asset and loaded by the linked app startup code; it is not a textual source passage.
Editable source artwork retained byte-for-byte from the v2 desktop asset. The runtime uses its existing PNG rendition.
